summary:
I made the frontend merge plan for groups 2 and 3 and checked it with a full trial merge in a scratch clone (<scratch> branch sim). No file under ~/Developer was changed, nothing was pushed, and nothing went to the network: npm ran with --offline and the Vite proxy pointed at a dead port.

**Files more than one branch changes:**
- frontend/src/game.js: G7, L2, Exchange v2, L5, A7.
- frontend/package.json: G7 scripts plus A4's dependency. It merges cleanly.
- frontend/main.js is changed by G7 only. A2/A3 adds four new files, and A6, S0 and open-world change nothing under frontend/.

**What git reports, in the fixed order:** 15 conflicting hunks, all in game.js: 1 at L2, 5 at Exchange v2, 4 at L5, 5 at A7. G7 and A4 merge with no frontend conflict, and G7's ASSETS.md and GRAPHICS.md merge cleanly with main.

**Resolution rule for every conflict:** keep the integration side, which already holds G7 and the earlier panels, and add only the incoming branch's own additions. The incoming side still has the old base lines and the old plot listener `on('plot_clicked'`, and taking them would drop G7's code.

**Three changes git will not show:**
1. hasOverlay must end with `caseUi.active||stopPlots.active,`. L2's islet-boundary.test.js reads game.js with a regex and checks this.
2. G7 no longer empties the container when the game shuts down. A7's panel only stops when its dialog leaves the container, so dispose() needs `container.querySelector('.duel-modal')?.remove();`. Without it the duel dialog stays open after shutdown; I confirmed this in a real browser.
3. Add the four panels to the isBlocked rule of G7's world experience, so the presence HUD hides while a panel is open (recommended).

**World check (`test:world`) changes:** it presses E at every hotspot.
- After L5 and A7 it fails for certain: it timed out right after the prediction kiosk.
- After group 2 it fails at random because of a lazy-load race at the islet plots: it failed at plot_2 in one run.
- Fix: a table of hotspot-to-panel pairs, close each panel before calling dismissIntro, and open the page with `?market=local&desk=local&arena=local` so no panel calls the API. With this it passed twice at the end of group 2 and twice at the end of group 3.

Escape needs no change. G7's handleEscape sends a 'cancel' to the open kit dialog, and each panel closes without the pause menu opening; I checked this in the browser.

**Packages:** A4's lock file has @supabase/supabase-js 2.118.0 and 8 dependencies. They are not installed in the integration worktree, but all 9 are in ~/.npm/_cacache, and `npm ci --offline` installed them in 3 s. It must run right after merging A4, or tests/realtime-library.test.js fails. A4's realtime client and A2's api.js and session.js are not imported by any code yet. They must stay out of the title chunk: it is 21,104 bytes against a 21,477-byte budget.

**Results on the fully merged tree:**
- `npm test`: 88 files, 1538 tests, about 7 s.
- `npm run build` with the spoiler guard: passes, about 4 s.
- Browser checks: world, islet, golden path, case, lifecycle, living, life, experience, browser, cinematics, readability, weather wiring, UI kit, loading, production and the highlights tour (171 s) all exit 0.
- `test:credits` and `test:chaos` fail at random; `test:credits` also does so on the unmerged G7 branch.
- `test:intro` needs a real API on port 8000.

**Spoiler leak already on main (needs a decision):** the production bundle contains the case fake's deduction table. It leaves exactly one of the four suspects uncleared, and that suspect is the culprit in the story round's secret case file. The fingerprint guard cannot see this. G7 adds a second way in from production (`?case=local&demo=1`).

**Ports:** the graphics worktree currently holds ports 5175, 5173 and 8000. Run browser checks one at a time with TEST_URL pointing at a dev server the agent started itself.

The resolved game.js after each merge step (L2, Exchange v2, L5, A7) and the matching check-world.js versions are in <scratch> The final game.js is game.after-a7.js.

RESOLUTION RULE (every conflict): start from the integration side (it already holds G7 and the earlier panels) and add only the incoming branch's own tokens.
